requirement:
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.

The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation maps to marked code and has a test.

**Location obligations**
- Unix uses `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when it is an absolute, nonempty path. This is `user_config_path_from` in `src/config.rs` (lines 688–701), using `absolute_directory`, which rejects an empty or relative value because an empty path is not absolute.
- Otherwise Unix uses `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`, taking `HOME` through `required_directory`.
- Windows uses `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`, taking `APPDATA` through `required_directory`.
- `HOME` and `APPDATA` must be absolute and nonempty. `required_directory` enforces this and returns an error otherwise.
- `ConfigPlatform::current` and `user_config_path` supply the real platform and the real environment.

**Failure obligation**
- `required_directory` returns `NotFound` with the message "cannot determine Habeas directory: {name} must be an absolute, nonempty path". That message names the variable.
- `resolve_authoring` (line 960) propagates this with `user_config_path()?`, so an operation that needs user configuration fails.

**Cross-project and project-independence obligations**
- `user_config_path` takes no project argument. It depends only on the platform and the environment. The location is therefore not chosen relative to a project and cannot be changed by project settings.
- The workspace file is loaded separately by `load_workspace_config(root)`, which is the `habeas.toml` path governed by `workspace_location`. I only checked that this call applies that requirement and did not reassess it.
- The MAY clause about user-local project preferences imposes nothing to check.

**Tests (`tests/configuration.rs`, both marked `{test}`)**
- `locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks` checks these cases:
  - an absolute XDG value;
  - an empty or relative XDG value falling back to `HOME/.config`;
  - Windows `APPDATA`;
  - the error when no variables are set.
- `base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty` checks these cases:
  - an empty or relative `HOME` or `APPDATA` produces an error that contains the variable name;
  - a relative XDG value falls back to an absolute `HOME`.

**Marking and unspecified behavior**
- I found no unmarked code that implements part of this requirement.
- I found no extra behavior beyond what the text specifies.
- The only other caller of `user_config_path`, `is_configuration_file` in `src/redaction.rs`, uses the path to recognize a file for redaction. It does not implement this requirement.

Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
